headline: Software Leads Broad Advance as Rate-Hike Fears Recede
body_html:
Thursday's session closed on a constructive note, with 303 of 549 names in our universe finishing higher as traders unwound bets on further rate increases. The dominant theme was unmistakable: software names surged to the front of the pack, with the sector posting a gain of 2.76%, while homebuilders added 1.54% and consumer stocks rose 0.82%. The advance was orderly rather than euphoric, reflecting a measured repricing of the rate path rather than outright risk-on exuberance.

Rotation cut sharply against cyclicals and chip stocks. Semiconductors shed 0.36% as a cluster of power and discrete names cratered on earnings-related pressure, and materials dropped 0.87%. Energy slipped 0.18% even as geopolitical headlines around the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi drone strikes on Gulf infrastructure kept crude risk elevated. The bifurcation between software's climb and the chip sector's stumble underscored how quickly the market can reprice winners and losers within technology itself.

The standout mover of the day was N-able, which surged 14.2% to lead all gainers in the universe — part of a broader software sweep that also lifted ZoomInfo, BlackLine, and Docusign each by more than 10%. On the other side of the ledger, Tapestry's 16.47% plunge was the session's sharpest single-name reversal. With breadth positive but not overwhelming, Thursday's tape reads less like a breakout and more like a careful repositioning ahead of the next catalyst.

briefs.headline: N-able Rockets 14% to Crown the Software Sweep
briefs.body: N-able posted the session's biggest gain at 14.2%, capping a remarkable day for cloud-software names broadly. ZoomInfo, BlackLine, and Docusign each climbed more than 10%, signaling that conviction behind enterprise software spending remains intact even as parts of the tech complex retreated. The cluster move suggests institutional rotation rather than isolated stock-specific news.

briefs.headline: Tapestry Suffers Session's Steepest Drop at 16%
briefs.body: Tapestry led all decliners Thursday, tumbling 16.47% in the apparel-luxury segment. The move stood out as the most violent single-name reversal of the session and dragged consumer-adjacent sentiment lower. YETI Holdings compounded the consumer pain, falling 10.57% and reinforcing pressure on discretionary brands facing demand uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Chip Names Split: Memory Soars While Power Semis Sink
briefs.body: Sandisk surged 13.67% even as the broader semiconductor sector fell 0.36%, illustrating a sharp divergence within the group. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor cratered 15.6% and Diodes dropped 9.2%, suggesting earnings or guidance disappointments among power and discrete chip makers. The memory-versus-analog divide was one of Thursday's clearest intraday fault lines.

briefs.headline: Cisco Drops 8% as Networking Stocks Feel the Squeeze
briefs.body: Cisco fell 8.4% and Coherent declined nearly 8%, making networking one of the session's worst-performing pockets despite the broader market's positive close. The paired selloff points to earnings or forward-guidance concerns weighing on companies exposed to enterprise and data-center infrastructure spending cycles. Neither decline appeared driven by the day's macro tailwinds.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Tensions Keep Energy Markets on Edge
briefs.body: Competing claims from Iran and the United States over control of the Strait of Hormuz, combined with Pentagon statements that a naval blockade on Iranian ports could be sustained indefinitely, kept geopolitical risk premiums elevated in energy markets. Houthi drone strikes on a Saudi Aramco refinery in Jazan added to supply-side anxiety, even as energy equities in our universe dipped 0.18% on the session.

briefs.headline: Rate-Hike Bets Retreat, Giving Equities Room to Breathe
briefs.body: Thursday's equity advance was anchored by a pullback in market expectations for additional rate increases, according to Reuters, with falling oil prices reinforcing the softer inflation read. Homebuilders, a sector acutely sensitive to the rate outlook, responded with a 1.54% gain — the second-best sectoral performance of the day. The move suggests rate-sensitive areas of the market remain tightly tethered to any shift in the policy narrative.
